title: Add an 'Estate' page to intentd that all intent-using Claudes on an estate can use to post status
objective: Give the host one live view of every Claude session on it: who it is, which project and node it stands in, whether it is busy, idle, in a heavy run or paused, its one-line WIP and its claims, with the host's load and the cargo and bats census. One source of truth on disk, a directory of session records under `~/.local/state/intent/estate/`, written by the sessions themselves through the hooks and the `intent estate` verbs; three renderers of it: intentd at `/estate/status` styled like top, `/estate` in the `intent explore` TUI beside `/projects`, and `intent estate status --json` for Claudes.
context: The estate is the host (rhadamanth, kovacs and gyges each its own), not a project; Intent, Devbin and Laksa are projects on it. Each project has a status surface already, the whiteboard, and what has no home is the layer above it: which sessions exist on the host, what each is doing, which heavy run holds the box. On 2026-10-24 that layer was run by hand over cross-session messages and a census script, and it vanished at every compact. intentd is one daemon per user with a web face and a registry of every project root on the host (ST0074), so it already knows the estate and renders none of it. State, not config: the records live under `~/.local/state/intent/estate/`, beside the daemon's own run dir, one writer per file, the readers never write, and the daemon reaps a record whose pid is dead. A session that is a whiteboard node does not copy its focus or claims into its record; the reader joins them from the project's store, so one fact has one home. The design is attached as `design.md`.

wps.title: The estate record and its doors: directory, versioned record, one reader, the estate verbs, the hooks writing presence, MCP exposure, the reap rule
intentd serves /estate/status: watches the estate directory outside the ingest path, renders the live top-styled page with the host census
The intent explore TUI: /estate beside /projects, on the same reader
Slots: a generic pool, ask, grant, start, release protocol on the estate, records beside the status records, capacity enforced by the tool, policy with the controlling Claude
wps.objective: A generic slot protocol on the estate with lanes and a named controller. The controller session, whichever session hv assigns, a dedicated one outside any project or a node inside one, takes control by writing `controller.json` (refused while a live holder's pid exists; a dead pid is succeeded) and declares lane types and lanes, each lane with a running capacity. Other sessions ask for a slot by lane type, the controller grants into a lane, denies or revokes, the holder starts and releases, and a grant over a lane's capacity is refused by the tool; policy beyond capacity stays with the controlling Claude. The records live beside the status records under `~/.local/state/intent/estate/slots/` (lanes, requests, the controller), each request a directory whose files are written one each by the acting party, so the state is the fold of the files and one writer per file holds. `slots wait` blocks a requester for its answer, `slots watch` streams state changes for the controller's monitor, and the UserPromptSubmit hook names pending asks to the controller. `intent estate init [<dir>]` renders a dedicated coordinator's working directory from Intent's own templates, contract and hook settings included, so the coordinator runs on Intent alone. The page and the TUI show the controller, every lane with its type, capacity, holders and queue, and each session's row shows the slots it holds.

# ST0086 design draft: the estate view

Written on 2026-10-24 from the rubber-duck between hv and vc. What is marked measured was measured; the rest is design to be measured before it is built.

## What it is

The estate is the host (rhadamanth, kovacs, gyges each its own). The estate view is a live top-styled table of every Claude session on the host: who it is, which project and node it stands in, whether it is busy, idle, in a heavy run or paused, its one-line WIP, its claims, and the host's load with the cargo and bats census. Three readers render one source of truth: intentd at /estate/status, the intent explore TUI at /estate, and `intent estate status --json` for Claudes.

## The source of truth

Presence and liveness are Claude Code's own session files, read and never written (hv's ruling, 2026-10-24). Claude Code writes `<config dir>/sessions/<pid>.json` for every session, where the config dir is `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or else `~/.claude` (measured on 2.1.310): `pid`, `procStart`, `sessionId`, `cwd`, `name` (the cross-session name), `status` (busy or idle), `startedAt`, `updatedAt` and `statusUpdatedAt` (epoch milliseconds), `messagingSocketPath`, `kind`, `entrypoint` and `version`. The format is not a published contract, so a reader test pins exactly the fields the reader relies on (pid, procStart, sessionId, cwd, name, status, startedAt, updatedAt), and a file that lacks one is shown as unreadable with the field named, never dropped. intentd runs under launchd, so the reader takes the config dir from the estate's own setting, not from the daemon's environment.

Intent adds only what that file lacks, and joins most of it rather than storing it. Project root is the Intent project whose tree holds the session's cwd. Node, focus and claims come from that project's store: the board whose recorded session id matches (`wb pickup` records it), which intentd (registry, ST0074) and the TUI already open. Paused is a board's paused status. Heavy is a running slot the session holds in any lane, a light lane included (see Slots and lanes), and gone is a dead pid (see Cleanup); neither is written by anyone (vc's ruling, 2026-10-24). Intent writes per session only what nothing else holds, in `~/.local/state/intent/estate/<session-id>.json`: a schema version (pinned from day one, since the dev, opt and brew switch lets two intents share a host), the session id, a WIP line for a session with no board, the statusline's latest `rate_limits` where that fallback is in use (see Readers), and the stamp the tool read at each write. It is written whole by atomic rename by that session alone, with no locking; it is state, not config (intentd's socket already lives under `~/.local/state/intent/run`, measured).

## Writers

Presence needs no Intent hook: Claude Code keeps its own session file current. The explicit verbs: `intent estate wip "<line>"` (a session with no board), `intent estate prune` (Intent's own WIP records only), and the slot verbs below. MCP exposes `status` and `wip` because a repeat changes nothing; the slot verbs accumulate and stay CLI.

## Readers

One reader function in intentsvcs returns the joined table from the directory plus the stores it points at; the page, the TUI pane and the verb are renderers of it (PFIC, thin coordinator). The daemon adds the host census (load, cargo and bats processes) it measures itself, which retires vc's census script.

The page is not a second document (vc's ruling, 2026-10-24): under D56 the daemon serves one shell document, so /estate/status is a route in `shell.html`, fed by `/op` with the reader's JSON, and the daemon renders no HTML for it. The mockup attached as `estate-status-mockup.html` shows the page's layout and the raw record shapes it reads (census, controller, lanes, requests with one key per file present, sessions, and the boards the reader joins), from an inline sample that re-renders on a timer. hv approved its layout on 2026-10-24: one band across the top (the host block, the last hour as sparklines of the 1-minute load and the running slots, and plan usage), then the queue as its own panel, oldest first, then the lanes, then the sessions. The sparklines need the daemon to keep a short in-memory ring of census samples (a minute apart, an hour long); it is not a record on disk and a restart starts it empty.

Plan usage comes from two sources, the second a fallback (hv's ruling, 2026-10-24: "1 is the fallback. But I think 2 is worth it."):

- Primary, the account's usage endpoint, as the claudecodeusage menubar app reads it (measured from its source). intentd reads Claude Code's OAuth access token from the macOS Keychain with `/usr/bin/security find-generic-password -s <service> -w`, whose service is `Claude Code-credentials`, suffixed with `-` and the first eight hex digits of the SHA-256 of the config dir when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, falling back to the unsuffixed name; the value is JSON and the token is `claudeAiOauth.accessToken`. It then sends `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`. The answer carries `five_hour` and `seven_day` (`utilization`, `resets_at`), `seven_day_sonnet`, the per-model weekly caps in a `limits` array (`scope.model.display_name`, `percent`, `resets_at`) and `extra_usage`. intentd reads it at most once a census tick and keeps the last answer in memory. The token is never written, logged or sent anywhere but that endpoint.
- Fallback, the statusline's `rate_limits` (measured on Claude Code 2.1.310): the JSON a session hands its statusline command carries an optional `rate_limits` with `five_hour` and `seven_day`, each `{used_percentage, resets_at}` in epoch seconds, for subscribers after the first API response, and no per-model figure. It is stdin to that command, not a file, so it reaches the estate only through a statusline step that writes the latest copy into the session's Intent record; defining that step is WP-02's.
- The failure path is named, never silent. When the Keychain read fails (no entry, access denied, a locked keychain), the endpoint answers anything but 200, or the answer will not parse, the page says which, shows the fallback's 5-hour and 7-day figures with their source and age, and marks per-model "unavailable" with the reason. With neither source it says "no source" and why. The Keychain is macOS only: elsewhere the fallback is the source until another platform's credential store is measured.

## Cleanup

A session file whose pid is dead, or whose pid now belongs to a process started at a different time than its `procStart`, renders as gone. Claude Code's files are never deleted by Intent; the daemon reaps only Intent's own WIP record for a gone session on its next tick, and `intent estate prune` does the same where no daemon runs. A live pid with an old `updatedAt` renders as idle with its age and is never reaped. A slot whose holder is gone renders as orphaned until its controller revokes it; a controller whose pid is dead leaves its record orphaned, and the next `control take` succeeds it. Readers never write.

## Slots and lanes

A generic way for one session to control how much of something runs at once and for others to ask for a share. Nothing in the tool knows what a lane is for; the names below (heavy, light, kovacs) are the ones 2026-10-24 ran by hand and are examples, not a fixed set.

- A lane type is a class the controller declares (heavy, light, kovacs). A lane is an instance of a type with its own running capacity: `intent estate slots lane open <lane> --type <type> --capacity <n>`; the same verb changes the capacity, and `lane close <lane>` ends it when nothing is granted in it. How many lanes, of which types, with what capacity, is the controller's call. On 2026-10-24 that was two heavy lanes of capacity one on the Mac (cargo, bats), one light lane beside bats, and one kovacs lane.
- A request asks by type, and may name a lane: `intent estate slots ask <type> "<what>" [--lane <lane>]` returns an id and queues it. Queued is per type. `slots wait <id>` blocks the requester until a grant or a denial lands, with a timeout.
- The controller: `grant <id> --lane <lane>`, `deny <id> "<why>"`, `revoke <id> "<why>"`. A grant that would put the lane over its capacity, counting granted and running, is refused and names the count; the controller raises the capacity if it means it. Which request goes first is the controller's judgement, never the tool's.
- The holder: `start <id>` and `release <id>`. `status` shows every lane with its type, capacity, holders and the queue for its type, and each session's row shows the slots it holds.
- The files are the protocol, under `~/.local/state/intent/estate/slots/`: `lanes/<lane>.json` written by the controller; each request a directory `requests/<id>/` holding `ask.json` from the requester, `grant.json` (naming the lane) or `deny.json` from the controller, `start.json` and `end.json` from the holder, `revoke.json` from the controller. A request belongs to no lane until granted. Its state is the fold of the files present (asked, granted, running, ended, denied, revoked), so one writer per file holds, no lock exists, and the readers read it like the session files.
- Learning without polling: `wait` for the requester; for a controller, the UserPromptSubmit hook names the pending asks on the lane types its session controls, the way it injects project context today.
- Out of the first cut: priorities, and any policy beyond capacity. Succession is by pid liveness only (see The coordinator).

## The coordinator

The controller is whichever session hv assigns to manage the workload: a dedicated session that stands in no Intent project, or a node inside one. The protocol treats both the same and names the role by a record instead of relying on a volunteer, which is what 2026-10-24 did.

- Control is a record: `intent estate control take` writes `controller.json` beside the lanes, one per host, with the session, its cross-session name and pid; `control release` ends it. A second take is refused while the holder's pid is alive; a dead pid leaves the record orphaned and a new take is allowed, which is the whole of succession in the first cut. Lane, grant, deny and revoke writes are accepted from the controller session only.
- The page and `status` show the controller at the top, or NO CONTROLLER, in which case asks queue and nothing is granted.
- Waking it: `intent estate slots watch` blocks and emits one line per state change under `slots/requests/` (asked, started, released), the shape a Monitor consumes, and the coordinator's contract arms it at session start. Requesters have `wait`, the coordinator has `watch`, and the UserPromptSubmit hook injects the pending asks on top.
- A dedicated coordinator stands in no project and has no node, so its WIP line is set directly; a project node that takes control keeps its project and node, and the reader joins its focus as for any node.
- All of it inside Intent, nothing else needed: `intent estate init [<dir>]` renders a dedicated coordinator's working directory from Intent's own templates (`lib/templates/estate/`, through the same token expander as every root file): its AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md carrying the coordinator contract (take control at session start, arm `slots watch` under a monitor, judge asks against lane capacity and the estate view, release control at session end), and `.claude/settings.json` wiring the same `intent claude hook` lifecycle hooks a project gets. A Claude Code session started in that directory is the coordinator with only Intent installed. A project node that is assigned control follows the same contract, carried to it by the hook injection.

## Work packages

- WP-01 the record and its doors: the reader of Claude Code's session files with the test pinning their fields, Intent's WIP record, the joins from the project stores, the verbs, MCP exposure, the reap rule.
- WP-02 the page: intentd watches the directories outside the ingest path and answers the reader over `/op`; /estate/status is a route in the one shell document (D56), live, top-styled, with the census and its ring, laid out as `estate-status-mockup.html`; plan usage from the endpoint with the statusline fallback and the named failure path.
- WP-03 the TUI: /estate in intent explore on the same reader, beside /projects.
- WP-04 slots, lanes and the coordinator: lane types and lanes with a capacity, the request records, the controller record with take and release, `intent estate init` and the coordinator templates, the slot verbs, the capacity refusal, wait and watch, the hook naming pending asks, and the controller, lanes and slots on the page and in the TUI.

## Out of scope

Cross-project announce; federation of estates across hosts (kovacs on rhadamanth's page); slot policy beyond capacity; anything a sleeve or dotfiles framework would add on top, since the coordinator runs on Intent alone.

## To measure before the design is final

- Whether intentd's watcher can take a directory outside any project without entering the ingest path (the ingest is what reverts the last write of a burst).
- What happens to a session's file when the session is killed rather than ended, so the pid and procStart rule is the backstop.
- The TUI's /projects reader, so /estate reuses its shape.
- Whether the Keychain read prompts when intentd, rather than Claude Code, asks for the item (the menubar app reads it through `/usr/bin/security` to stay inside the item's access list).
- The `/usage` output, which was not measured.

Resolved on 2026-10-24: the cross-session name is in Claude Code's own session file, so no hook has to see it; plan usage's sources and Claude Code's session files, by hv's rulings above.
